name: restore_state_and_cleanup

name: launch_workbench_tool_task
description: Checks for a resident Workbench task and, when a tool is to be started, allocates a 162-byte block, copies a global command string into it and calls the library routines that launch the tool. Failure paths report a 'cannot start tool' message with the error number.

name: compare_zero_terminated_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte, returning minus one if the first is smaller at the first difference, one if it is larger and zero when they match.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of entries, allocating an eight-byte node for each through the library and storing a value obtained from the entry in the node's second field, with nodes chained by shifted pointers. It returns the head of the chain, or whatever was built before a failure.

name: invoke_library_vector_132
description: Calls a library function through a vector at a fixed negative offset from a library base kept in a global variable, with no arguments and no result.

name: invoke_library_vector_138

name: pad_release_string_on_match

name: write_dot_and_four_spaces

name: skip_matching_prefix
description: Advances through a buffer for as long as its bytes match a stored string, stopping at the end of that string or at the first difference, and returns with the pointer moved past the matched prefix.

name: stub_empty_return

name: page_file_with_progress_display
description: Takes a file name from the arguments or prompts for one, then displays the file a page at a time in a window with a percentage progress indicator and a quit hint. It warns when the file looks binary and reports end-of-file or not-found conditions.

name: call_routine_for_four_globals
description: Calls a routine four times in turn, passing a fixed field of a structure together with each of four consecutive global values.

name: validate_input_buffer
description: Calls two routines to fill an eighty-byte block of a buffer, then returns one as soon as it finds a byte within the first eighty that is a control character other than the usual text controls, or a value in the 128 to 159 range. It returns zero when all eighty bytes pass.

name: read_console_key_and_dispatch
description: Waits for a console event, reads one key code and dispatches it through a switch: it skips escape-sequence bodies, handles a few navigation and quit codes, and returns a result code. A break signal sets a marker field to minus one and returns zero.

name: call_setup_then_register_handler
description: Passes a global value to one routine, calls a second routine, then invokes a code pointer held in an address register and returns.

name: initialize_state_and_run_steps
description: Initializes two fields of a state structure and stores the result of a routine call in another field. It then calls a routine and repeats a step while a counter is positive and a pair of 16-bit values in a linked structure show work remaining.

name: update_entity_and_increment_counter
description: Calls a routine twice, passing the second result along, and stores the final result in a field of the structure. When a flag field is zero it increments a 16-bit counter in a structure reached through a pointer.

name: read_line_marking_form_feed
description: Reads up to 128 bytes into a buffer and counts the characters before the first newline or form feed. A form feed is replaced by the two characters caret and L followed by a newline and sets a flag, the buffer is terminated, and the count is returned.

name: process_entries_with_quit_check
description: Chooses a loop limit of nine, thirteen or fourteen from a flag and a field, then processes queued entries from a global table through a routine until the limit is reached. After each pass it reads a key and calls a routine to stop when the input is q or a break code.

name: search_until_match
description: Sets up a search and repeatedly steps through it until a routine reports a match, returning one on a match and zero when the counter check fails first.

name: run_call_sequence_return_result
description: Runs a fixed sequence of routine calls on a parameter block, passing a global value and the first argument at one step, and returns the result of the call that uses both parameters.

name: check_flag_and_call
description: Calls a routine with its first two arguments, then calls a second routine with the first argument only when a 16-bit flag in a structure is zero.

name: call_stored_value_then_forward
description: Calls a routine with a stored field, a minus-one argument and a pointer, then calls a second routine with a 16-bit value read from a linked structure.

name: call_fixed_then_forward_decremented
description: Calls a routine with a zero argument and the constant one, then calls a second routine with a 16-bit value from a linked structure reduced by one.

name: emit_text_lines_to_handler
description: Walks a text buffer line by line, counting characters per line up to a limit taken from a structure and passing each segment through a handler routine. It stops after the requested number of lines, at a form feed, or when a flag is set.

name: process_then_dispatch_via_pointer
description: Calls a routine with its second argument, then calls another routine using a pointer taken from a structure, a global variable and the first argument.

name: set_flag_and_forward
description: When a field of a structure is zero, sets a 16-bit field of the structure reached through a pointer to one. It then calls a routine with a structure pointer and a global pointer.

name: dispatch_by_flag
description: Calls a routine with a global pointer and a third argument chosen by a flag in the parameter block: either a global pointer, or a 16-bit value from a linked structure plus one.

name: dispatch_handler_by_flag
description: Calls a routine with a global pointer repeated three times when a flag in the parameter block is zero. Otherwise it passes a single global pointer and a 16-bit value from a linked structure.

name: clamp_negative_result
description: Calls a routine twice with the same first argument and different third arguments, then returns the second result with negative values clamped to zero.

name: consume_from_buffer
description: Copies up to a requested number of bytes from the structure's buffer into a destination, clamped to the bytes still remaining, after first refilling the buffer when it is short. It advances the offset and position fields, reduces the remaining count, and returns the number taken.

name: refill_buffer_keeping_remainder
description: When unread bytes remain and the buffer is full, moves those bytes to the front of the buffer, then reads more data into the free space through a routine. It clears the offset field, copies saved values between fields and returns the routine's result.

name: update_window_bounds_and_position
description: Computes a target position from an offset and one of three modes: absolute, relative to the current position, or relative to a stored value. It checks the target against the window bounds, updating position, size and offset fields and calling routines to reset or move the window when it falls outside. It returns the stored position, or minus one for an unknown mode.

name: read_line_from_buffer
description: Reads bytes one at a time from a source into a destination, storing the newline if one arrives, and stops after a newline or after about 127 bytes. It terminates the text and returns the number of bytes counted before the stop.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination until the null terminator has been copied.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Converts each lowercase ASCII letter in a zero-terminated string to uppercase by subtracting the case offset, leaving other bytes unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal_string
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign and then a run of decimal digits, accumulating them into an integer and negating the result for a minus sign.

name: call_with_mask_if_set
description: When the first argument is non-zero and a pointer in a structure is set, calls a routine with that pointer, the first argument and a minus-one argument.

name: process_text_and_free_structure
description: Calls routines on the structure's fields, then handles its text: when the flag is set and the text is non-empty, it reads characters until a newline arrives. It copies pending values back into the structure, releases optional sub-objects, and finally frees the structure block of a fixed size.

name: pass_single_value_to_handler
description: Stores its argument in a one-element stack buffer and passes it, with a constant of 994 and a size of one, to a routine that takes its target from a pointer in a global structure. It returns that routine's result.

name: allocate_pass_and_copy_fields
description: Allocates a 36-byte block and passes its shifted pointer through a routine together with a constant of 25. It copies a field and a value reached through a pointer in the block into the caller's structure, releases the block and returns the result of the pass.

name: build_template_block_return_field
description: Allocates a 68-byte block, links it to itself and stores a template value and a parameter in it, then copies a number of words from a source into the block. It registers the block through a routine, reads one field, then releases the block and returns that field, or zero when a lookup or allocation fails.

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor: for divisors above 65535 it runs a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract division, and otherwise it divides the two halves of the value by the 16-bit divisor. It returns the remainder and quotient packed together.

name: multiply_32bit_with_partial_products
description: Computes the low 32 bits of a 32-bit multiplication from four 16-bit partial products and returns them together with the second operand with its two halves swapped.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and then returns.

name: negate_result_on_flag
description: Calls a routine and returns its result, negated when the routine leaves a non-zero value in an address register.

name: invoke_exec_rawdofmt
description: Calls the RawDoFmt function of the exec library through a stored library base, using arguments already in place.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the memory address held in an address register and returns.

name: allocate_signal_block_and_dispatch
description: Obtains a signal bit through a routine, then allocates a 34-byte block and fills its fields with the parameters, the signal bit and a value from another routine. It passes the block to one of two routines, or releases the signal bit and returns zero when the allocation fails.

name: remove_and_free_signal_block
description: Removes the block from its list when it is linked, marks its status fields as deleted, releases its signal bit and frees the 34-byte block.

name: find_substring_in_text
description: Searches a zero-terminated text for a zero-terminated pattern, returning one when the pattern occurs and zero otherwise. It returns zero for an empty pattern or a text that starts with a newline.

name: initialize_list_header
description: Initializes a list header in place: its first word points to the word after it, its second word is cleared, and its third word points back to the header.

name: release_format_resources
description: Releases each allocated resource in turn, freeing a 260-byte buffer and a 36-byte block when they are present, then passes the status argument to a final routine.

name: map_disk_error_to_message
description: Runs a disk operation and retries it while the operation reports one specific code. It then maps the result to a text message for known faults, such as a bad sector, a seek error, a missing disk or an unopenable device, and returns the code.

name: report_format_status
description: Outputs one of two status messages chosen by a flag and returns the status code as a number. The fixed path makes three output calls, and the other path outputs a single stored value.

name: record_matching_table_entry
description: Searches an eight-entry global table for the given byte and stores the matching entry, or zero when none matches, into a field of a block obtained from a routine. It returns the argument unchanged.

name: find_matching_list_entry
description: Walks a linked list of entries and returns one when it finds an entry matching the given value, either by a stored value or by a comparison routine applied to a name. It performs follow-up calls with the matching entry, and returns zero when the list ends without a match.

name: calculate_string_length
description: Counts the bytes of a zero-terminated string up to the terminator and returns that count.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination until the null terminator has been copied.

name: convert_char_to_uppercase
description: Returns the uppercase form of a single byte when it is a lowercase ASCII letter, and the byte unchanged otherwise.

name: compare_strings_ignoring_case
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings after converting each byte to uppercase, returning one when they are equal and zero otherwise.

name: truncate_string_at_colon
description: Walks a string up to its first colon or terminator and writes a zero byte there, truncating the string before the colon.

name: pass_value_and_map_failure

description: Allocates a 68-byte block, links it to itself and stores a template value and a parameter in it, then copies a number of words from a source into the block. It registers the block through a routine, reads one field, then releases the block and returns that field, or zero when a lookup or allocation fails.

name: format_disk_track_by_track
description: Formats the disk one cylinder at a time: it obtains a disk port and a track buffer, fills each sector's header words with a DOS identifier, the sector number and the cylinder number, then writes and verifies the track. It prints a progress line per cylinder, puts a COPY marker at the start of the first cylinder's buffer and returns a status code.

name: configure_handle_then_forward
description: Makes three calls on a handle held in a global structure, passing the constants twenty and thirty, then one, then forwards its parameter together with a value returned by another routine.

name: measure_stack_string_and_forward
description: Calls a stored library function, then measures the length of a 140-byte stack buffer up to its terminator. If the length is non-zero it passes the buffer and the length to another routine.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the memory address held in an address register and returns.

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor: for divisors above 65535 it runs a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract division, and otherwise it divides the two halves of the value by the 16-bit divisor. It returns the remainder and quotient packed together.

name: run_sixteen_step_division
description: Runs a sixteen-step restoring division loop that shifts the dividend's halves together and subtracts the divisor whenever the partial remainder reaches it. It leaves its working values in registers and returns nothing.

name: multiply_32bit_with_partial_products
description: Computes the low 32 bits of a 32-bit multiplication from four 16-bit partial products and returns them together with the second operand with its two halves swapped.

name: invoke_exec_rawdofmt
description: Calls the RawDoFmt function of the exec library through a stored library base, using arguments already in place.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the memory address held in an address register and returns.

name: allocate_signal_block_and_dispatch
description: Obtains a signal bit through a routine, then allocates a 34-byte block and fills its fields with the parameters, the signal bit and a value from another routine. It passes the block to one of two routines, or releases the signal bit and returns zero when the allocation fails.

name: remove_and_free_signal_block
description: Removes the block from its list when it is linked, marks its status fields as deleted, releases its signal bit and frees the 34-byte block.

name: forward_param_with_constant
description: Forwards its parameter to another routine together with the constant 48, then returns.

name: forward_single_param
description: Forwards its parameter unchanged to another routine, then returns.

name: setup_trashcan_drawer_globals
description: Saves a field, sets it to a sentinel while it fills several global values, then calls routines that use them. The text refers to a Trashcan path. It restores the saved field and returns a status value.

name: read_byte_or_minus_one
description: Calls a routine to read one byte into a small stack buffer. It returns that byte, sign-extended, when the call reports exactly one byte, and minus one otherwise.

name: invoke_library_vector_240
description: Calls a library function through a vector at a fixed negative offset from a library base kept in a global variable, with no arguments and no result.

name: initialize_list_header
description: Initializes a list header in place: its first word points to the word after it, its second word is cleared, and its third word points back to the header.

name: allocate_node_with_fields
description: Allocates a block of the requested size and, when that succeeds and a pointer is supplied, stores a byte value of five, the low word of the size argument and the pointer into fixed offsets of the block. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: reset_node_then_pass_on
description: Returns zero for a null pointer. Otherwise it sets a byte field to 255, sets two longword fields to minus one, and passes the pointer with a 16-bit field of the node to another routine, returning that routine's result.

name: invoke_library_vector_90

name: start_program_cli_or_wb
description: Allocates a control block through exec, then branches: when started from the Workbench it takes the startup message, and when started from the CLI it splits the command line into an argument table, honouring double quotes and asterisk escapes for newline and escape characters. It then calls a routine, releases the block and returns the stored status.

name: invoke_exec_supervisor

name: invoke_exec_exitintr

name: invoke_exec_switch

name: invoke_exec_dispatch

name: invoke_exec_makefunctions

name: invoke_exec_findresident

name: invoke_exec_enable

name: invoke_exec_allocentry

name: start_cli_session_with_scripts
description: Allocates a 64-byte command-line structure and fills in its fields, then sets up a console window from either a default specification or one given on the command line. It runs the CLI and Shell startup scripts from the S: directory when they exist, and returns the resulting value.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of entries, allocating an eight-byte node for each through the library and storing a value obtained from the entry in its second field, with nodes chained by shifted pointers. It returns the head of the chain as a shifted pointer, or the chain built so far when a step fails.
